report.summary: The change adds +1 to nextOffset in page(), which skips one issue or comment at every page boundary. Spec 09 says to follow nextOffset until it is null, and the item at offset+bounded.length is never returned. The existing worker test expects nextOffset 2 after a 2-item first page, so it now fails, and the second page gets only 1 item instead of 2.

findings.text: Off-by-one in nextOffset: each page boundary skips one entry, so agents paging through list_issues or list_issue_comments silently miss data.

evidence.quote: nextOffset: bounded.length < items.length || items.length === 50 ? offset + bounded.length + 1 : null,
evidence.why: A page returns the entries at offset through offset+bounded.length-1, so the next unread entry is at offset+bounded.length. Adding 1 skips it. The handler offset is a plain skip count, as spec 09 line 99 says ('Offset must be a nonnegative safe integer'). Example: 4 comments of about 65 KB, where the byte bound fits 2 per page. The first page returns items 0-1 with nextOffset 3, and the second page returns only item 3, so item 2 is lost. With a full page of 50, the next offset is 51 and item 50 is skipped. apps/tempo/test/worker/agent-issues.cases.ts:296 `expect(first.nextOffset).toBe(2);` and the 4-unique-ids assertion both fail. Spec 09 line 107 says 'follow `nextOffset` until it is null', which only works when nothing is skipped.

checked.risk: Real contracts: offset semantics of the repository list handlers and the MCP tool page contract
Failure paths / idempotency: whether pagination loses work when an agent follows nextOffset
Tests: existing pagination test against the new behavior
Spec: behavior compared with spec 09 for the tempo MCP tools; no spec change in the diff
Security, build and runtime environment: not affected by a one-line arithmetic change; no secrets, images or permissions touched
